_comment: Curated starting points for local inference via Ollama, not an exhaustive
registry — Ollama publishes no API for browsing its library, so this list
is maintained by hand and is meant to be edited.
size_mb is the approximate on-disk/in-memory footprint of the default
quantization Ollama pulls for that tag. Treat it as a sizing hint, not a
guarantee: quantization choices move these numbers considerably.
Verify a tag exists before relying on it: `ollama show <tag>`.

models.name: Qwen3.5 0.8B
models.good_for: Smoke-testing the pipeline on any machine, including a Pi.

models.name: Qwen3.5 4B
models.good_for: Fast replies on a laptop with no dedicated GPU.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.good_for: General chat and images on modest hardware. A sensible floor.

models.name: Ornith 9B
models.good_for: Agentic coding on an 8 GB GPU. Pairs well with the gateway.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.good_for: The default chat model: strong for its size, 256K context.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B
models.good_for: Tool use and reasoning; OpenAI's open-weight model.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B
models.good_for: The strongest local coding model a 24 GB GPU can hold.

models.name: Qwen3.6 35B (MoE)
models.good_for: Fast for its size: only a few billion parameters are active per token.

models.name: gpt-oss 120B
models.good_for: Workstation-class reasoning. Needs 80 GB of memory or more.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.good_for: Frontier open weights. Needs a server, not a desktop — most people should reach it through an API provider instead.
